full_query: A 27-year-old man presents for an appointment to establish care. He recently was released from prison. He has felt very fatigued and has had a cough. He has lost roughly 15 pounds over the past 3 weeks. He attributes this to intravenous drug use in prison. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. QuantiFERON gold testing is positive. The patient is started on appropriate treatment. Which of the following is the most likely indication to discontinue this patient's treatment? (A) Elevated liver enzymes (B) Hyperuricemia (C) Optic neuritis (D) Peripheral neuropathy (E) Red body excretions

sentences: To answer this question, we need to consider the adverse effects of antituberculosis medications and their implications on treatment discontinuation
The patient has tested positive for tuberculosis (TB) (QuantiFERON gold testing positive) and has been started on appropriate treatment
Antituberculosis drugs, especially isoniazid, rifampin, and pyrazinamide, are known to cause hepatotoxicity
Elevated liver enzymes may indicate hepatotoxicity, which is a significant adverse effect that could warrant discontinuation of the medications until liver function normalizes
Pyrazinamide is associated with causing hyperuricemia
While hyperuricemia can be uncomfortable, it typically does not necessitate discontinuation of treatment unless it leads to symptomatic gout or severe uric acid nephropathy
Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, which manifests as visual disturbances and can lead to permanent vision loss if not addressed promptly
This is a serious adverse effect and is indeed an indication for discontinuation of ethambutol to prevent permanent damage
Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy due to pyridoxine (vitamin B6) deficiency
This can often be prevented or managed by supplementing pyridoxine, and typically does not require discontinuation of isoniazid unless symptoms are severe
Rifampin can cause red-orange discoloration of body fluids (e.g., urine, sweat, saliva)
This is a benign side effect and does not necessitate discontinuation of treatment
Given the above considerations, the most likely indication to discontinue this patient's treatment would be optic neuritis
